Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Goal 2 Playing area 3 Orders 4 Crystals 5 Actions Goal Deliver crystals to your base. The first player to get 10 or more points immediately wins. Different amount of players slightly changes the score needed for win. Playing area The game is for 2-6 players. In case of 5 or 6 players, the larger playing area is used. Tiles are hexagonal. Orders You take control of two bots. Each has space for up to three orders. These orders allow you to move the bot; turn it left and right; and load and unload crystals. There are also some special orders. Each player has one special order at the beginning of the game. Each turn all issued orders are executed, first of your bot A, then bot B. No orders (beside Double Modification ) are ever consumed, they stay in the list of orders of given bot until you modify it. Moving forward will push both crystals and bots if there is empty tile to push to. Bots can push only one object at a time unless they are using special order Dash. Bases can't be pushed. Your bots can load crystals from other bots and any bot can deliver to any base. You can also zap bots, both yours and enemy ones to make them do one basic order of your liking. Crystals Crystals delivered to your base give you blue - 2 points + random special order green - 3 points red - 4 points When the game ends, you also score one point less than the core value per each crystal still carried by your bots. (1 for blue, 2 for green, and 3 for red) New crystals will spawn in the central tile when crystals get delivered. If that tile is full, the player to whose base the last crystal got delivered to can pick one of the adjacent tiles. If those are also full, the placement circle enlarges again until there is an open option. Actions Each turn you can pick from one of these actions to modify the orders of your bots: Keep the current orders - select this option in the upper ribbon Add one order - click unused order, click unused order space Change one order - click unused order, click used order Delete one order - click used order, click X under it Swap two orders of one bot - click used order, click used order Delete all orders of one bot - click X under bot In the first turn you can do two actions. Additionally, once per game you can do two actions in any turn. For that, do the first action, select the Double Modification order, then do the second one. The Double Modification order is consumed during this process. At game setup, there is the option to add some special tiles randomly to the board: Rocks - immovable obstacles Blobs - movable obstacles. These can be moved to any of the adjacent tiles by zapping, and can be pushed this way Teleporters - crystals or bots that get on teleport tile from one direction appear in the same direction from the tile of the other same-coloured teleport Mud - subtracts one from movement Board Game Arena would like to thank Flatlined Games for making it possible to have this game here. 1009 twintinbots العربية беларуская мова български език Brezhoneg Català čeština Dansk Deutsch Ελληνικά English Español Eesti keel فارسی Suomi Français Galego עברית Hrvatski Magyar Italiano Bahasa Indonesia 日本語 한국어 Lietuvių Latviešu Bahasa Malaysia Nederlands Norsk Polski Português Română Русский язык Slovenčina Slovenščina Српски Svenska ไทย Türkçe Українська мова Tiếng Việt 中文 (漢) 中文 (汉) Application loading... ... {DISPLAY_IN_OTHER_LANG} {LANG_REDIRECT_CODE} boardgamearena.com Top Help What is Board Game Arena? [Rating: 1/10] A programming game that I just really did not enjoy. Also, stealing crystals is rather difficult so pulling that off is quite a nice highlight.

[Rating: 2/10] Game on programming robots that does not work. Main twist is that you can every turn only slightly alter the programming of your robots. In my opinion players feel impotent, but don't experience the fun of the randomness from RoboRally.

[Rating: 2/10] What a piece of turd. A total toilet. Programming games are fun in general but those games have something in common. You cannot fully anticipate everything. They also move fast.   Twin Tin Bots is super slow and all too predictable to be any fun. This is because you're making only small changes to the program each round. This results in long stretches of time when nothing interesting happens. And this waiting is what ruins the game. Hate it. Not the worst experience I've ever had but close.

[Rating: 2/10] Wonder why they went with only 1 new order allowed per turn when 2 would make the game much less slow and tedious. Presumably to give some feeling of inertia and chaos but unfortunately I think it’s not a success.

[Rating: 3/10] When I heard about this game's premise I was very excited to play it. The simultaneous programming of two robots to achieve some amazing choreography seemed like it would be glorious. However what ended up happening is everyone concentrating on making good use of one robot while letting the other repeatedly bump into a corner. This completely invalidated the main draw of the game.  Unless you have genius levels of forward planning capabilities you're simply much better off plyaing Robo Rally

[Rating: 3/10] programming robots sounds great, but I found this game very boring [+] the special orders maybe... [-] too long for what it is (even online), for me it took a couple plays to 'get' it (which is OK), BUT even then, I did not enjoy the time playing the game  play on BGA

[Rating: 3/10] Sadly, not my cup of tea.  But it has taught me why some gamers find RoboRally tedious, which is a potentially valuable lesson.

[Rating: 3/10] You have two robots with three programble actions, but you can only change one action each turn. That's of course the challenge of the game, but it feels very limiting to me.

[Rating: 3/10] Players have a pair of robots which they preprogram to move and collect crystals. Each robot has 3 slots to program, and the trick is that you can only change one order on one robot. The orders are rotate, move, collect gems, etc. First player to collect a certain value of gems wins.  I have a few beefs about this game: 1) There is no balancing factor for players going last in the turn order. 2) It can be chaotic with more players.  At least it isn't a long game. The result is robots that go in circles or bump into objects/walls because you can only really focus on one robot per round.
